ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Swami Vivekananda Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: New patient visit for thirst, frequent urination, tiredness and weight loss in a 35-year-old monk told of diabetes a year ago and never tested: examination, random glucose and urine tests, and planning of fasting tests to confirm and classify diabetes; long-standing insomnia; raised blood pressure. Concerns: He is thirsty, up at night to pass urine, tired and losing weight, and wants to know whether he truly has diabetes and what kind; He wants any treatment to fit his monastic life: his diet, his fasts and his travel; He has never been able to fall asleep easily, and broken nights now leave him exhausted. [S]

tr.td: Comprehensive diabetic foot examination: skin intact; pulses present; 10-g monofilament and vibration sense normal at all sites
Diabetes self-management education and medical nutrition therapy referral: a dietitian visit to build a meal plan around his monastery diet and fasts
Advance care planning conversation, about 20 minutes, with his consent
Diabetic retinopathy screening with retinal photographs of both eyes: no retinopathy; no macular edema
Chest X-ray, posteroanterior and lateral: mild hyperinflation; heart size normal; no pulmonary edema, effusion or consolidation
Resting 12-lead ECG: sinus tachycardia at 106 per minute; normal axis and intervals; no ischemic change

Spirometry before and 15 minutes after albuterol 400 mcg, with FeNO, interpreted with GLI Global race-neutral equations: FEV1 2.95 L (77 percent predicted) rising to 3.42 L (+470 mL, +16 percent); FEV1/FVC 0.66 before and 0.75 after; FeNO 44 ppb. Reversible airflow obstruction: asthma
Written asthma action plan with peak flow zones (green above 470 L/min, yellow 300 to 470, red below 300, from his predicted value until a personal best is set), given and explained
Inhaler technique with a spacer, taught and checked by teach-back: correct
COVID-19 mRNA vaccine, this season's formula
Tdap vaccine (no record of a tetanus vaccine in adulthood)

list.item: Thirst, frequent urination day and night, tiredness and about 4 kg weight loss over two months, with a random glucose of 246 mg/dL; told by physicians a year ago that he had diabetes, never confirmed with modern tests or treated except by diet. Diabetes to be confirmed and classified (type 2, type 1 or slowly progressive autoimmune diabetes) with A1c, fasting glucose, GAD antibodies and C-peptide: resolved, confirmed [S]

Type 2 diabetes: A1c 9.4 percent and fasting glucose 172 mg/dL, with symptoms; GAD65 antibodies negative and fasting C-peptide preserved (2.6 ng/mL); no ketones. BMI 24.6, in the range where ADA screens Asian Americans. Classified as type 2, not type 1 or slowly progressive autoimmune diabetes: active, confirmed [S]
Moderately increased albuminuria on a first sample (urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 46 mg/g), eGFR normal; to be confirmed on two of three samples over three to six months: resolved, confirmed [S]
Raised blood pressure in clinic (138/86, average of two readings) without a diagnosis of hypertension; home readings to be taken: resolved, confirmed [S]
Hypertension, stage 1: clinic 138/86, 136/86 and 134/84; home average 136/86 over seven days; with moderately increased albuminuria and diabetes: active, confirmed [S]

Long-standing difficulty falling asleep: by his own account he has never been able to fall asleep on getting into bed and lies awake for two hours or more most nights; worse lately with waking to pass urine; rises before dawn for meditation: active, confirmed [S]
Mixed hyperlipidemia: LDL cholesterol 132 mg/dL, triglycerides 228, HDL 36: active, confirmed [S]

Attacks of wheeze and breathlessness for three weeks since coming down from the mountains to the damp plains, the worst last night with a sense of suffocation: peak flow 330 L/min (56 percent of predicted), oxygen saturation 94 percent, rising to 410 L/min after bronchodilator; no fever, edema or chest pain; chest X-ray and ECG without heart failure or pneumonia. Asthma to be confirmed with spirometry: resolved, confirmed [S]

Asthma, adult onset, confirmed: FEV1 2.95 L (77 percent predicted) rising 470 mL (16 percent) after bronchodilator, FEV1/FVC 0.66 rising to 0.75; FeNO 44 ppb; brought on by damp air and smoke; one moderate attack treated with prednisone: active, confirmed [S]
Diabetic kidney disease, CKD stage G1 A2: moderately increased albuminuria on three samples over eight months (46, 41 and 34 mg/g) with eGFR above 90: active, confirmed [S]

list.item: A Hindu monk of a monastic order, under vows of renunciation and celibacy; head of the order and of its service mission; lives at the order's monastery by the river with his brother monks and young disciples; teaches daily classes on scripture and lectures widely [S]

Daily routine: rises before dawn for meditation and worship; teaching and correspondence through the day; often works late into the night. Travels often, in India and abroad, and is now planning a long journey in the mountains from the spring [S]

Diet: eats with the monastery, mostly vegetarian (rice, chapati, dal, vegetables, milk and yogurt, and sweets offered after worship), with fish at some meals by his own choice; keeps religious fasts on the eleventh day of each lunar fortnight and at major festivals, sometimes without water. A year ago he believed that eating only meat and drinking no water was the way to live with diabetes [S]
No alcohol, by his vows; no tobacco use now; no drug use. Incense and smoke from the monastery kitchen fires [S]
Supports: his brother monks and disciples, who share his daily life; his faith and practice. He wants his care to fit his vows and his duties, and he alone decides it [S]

tr.td: New patient visit for thirst, frequent urination, tiredness and weight loss in a 35-year-old monk told of diabetes a year ago and never tested: examination, random glucose and urine tests, and planning of fasting tests to confirm and classify diabetes; long-standing insomnia; raised blood pressure

Diagnosis visit with the endocrinology consultation: A1c, fasting glucose, GAD antibodies, C-peptide, urine albumin, lipids and B12; type 2 diabetes confirmed; metformin by shared decision; nutrition and fasting plans

Five-week diabetes review before a long journey: glucose log, metformin dose, kidney function and potassium on losartan, repeat urine albumin, retinal photographs, statin, and a travel and fasting plan

Review after seven months away and a week after an asthma attack: A1c, kidneys, lipids, spirometry with bronchodilator response and FeNO; asthma and diabetic kidney disease confirmed; empagliflozin and maintenance-and-reliever inhaler; fasting plan for the coming festival
Same-day sick visit for an asthma attack after returning from the mountains

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Endocrinology consultation in one week, the same day as fasting blood tests, to confirm and classify diabetes (A1c, fasting glucose, GAD antibodies, C-peptide), and advise on treatment that fits his diet, his religious fasts and his travel

Diagnostic tests in one week, fasting: A1c, fasting plasma glucose, GAD65 antibodies, C-peptide, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, lipid panel, ALT, TSH and vitamin B12; urine ketones negative today; drink water freely while thirsty and avoid waterless fasts until the results are known; return the same day if vomiting, abdominal pain or drowsiness
Home blood pressure readings twice daily for a week with a validated upper-arm cuff, because clinic readings are raised

Insomnia: sleep diary for two weeks, screening for sleep apnea, and cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia adapted to his pre-dawn meditation; no sleeping tablets, by his preference; nocturia to be reviewed once glucose is treated

Metformin extended-release with the evening meal, titrated to 2000 mg, chosen by shared decision over early combination therapy or an injected GLP-1 receptor agonist; home glucose meter; diabetes education and medical nutrition therapy for a mostly vegetarian plan built on his monastery meals, his choices and his fasts; sulfonylureas avoided because of fasting

Religious fasting plan adapted from IDF-DAR risk stratification: fasts with fruit, milk and water allowed; waterless fasts only once glucose is steady, with hydration; metformin with the meal that ends the fast; glucose checks at midday and before breaking the fast; break the fast below 70 or above 300 mg/dL or when unwell
Vaccines for an adult with diabetes: influenza and COVID-19 each season, PCV20 once, hepatitis B (two doses) and Tdap
Hypertension with albuminuria: losartan 25 mg daily (an ARB rather than an ACE inhibitor, to avoid cough), less salt, home readings, potassium and creatinine two weeks after starting
Cardiovascular prevention: atorvastatin 10 mg daily at 35 with diabetes, South Asian ancestry, albuminuria and hypertension, by his choice; lipid panel six to twelve weeks after starting

Travel plan for months away: medicine and test-strip supply, sick-day rules (hold metformin and losartan when vomiting, with diarrhea or unable to drink), monthly messages with readings, and A1c, urine albumin and lipids at three months wherever he is

Asthma attack in a man with diabetes: prednisone 40 mg for five days with glucose checks before breakfast and the evening meal and a call for readings above 300 mg/dL; as-needed budesonide-formoterol until spirometry; review within a week

Diabetic kidney disease G1 A2: empagliflozin 10 mg each morning, skipped on waterless fast days and stopped with metformin when unable to eat or drink; losartan continued; potassium, creatinine and urine albumin in three months, then every six months

Asthma on GINA track 1, step 3: budesonide-formoterol one inhalation twice daily and as needed with a spacer, a written action plan, a smoke-free room, review in four to six weeks and spirometry in three months
